question: In the parasympathetic system:

options.opa: The preganglionic neuron is in thoracic spinal cord.
options.ope: Numerous neurons innervate vascular smooth muscle of the extremities.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Parasympathetic system" -> "Preganglionic neurons originate in the brainstem and sacral spinal cord" -> "Not in thoracic spinal cord" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Parasympathetic system" -> "Postganglionic neurons are located near or in target organs" -> "Postganglionic neurons have short axons" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Parasympathetic system" -> "Postganglionic fibers release acetylcholine" -> "Not noradrenaline" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Postganglionic neurons" -> "Have receptors for acetylcholine" -> "Muscarinic receptors present" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Parasympathetic system" -> "Primarily innervates organs" -> "Not vascular smooth muscle of extremities" -> "Unclear" -> 70%
analysis: In the parasympathetic nervous system, the preganglionic neurons originate in the brainstem and sacral spinal cord, not the thoracic spinal cord. Postganglionic neurons typically have long axons, not short. Postganglionic fibers release acetylcholine, not noradrenaline. Muscarinic receptors are found on the target organs, not on postganglionic neurons themselves. The parasympathetic system does not innervate vascular smooth muscle of the extremities, which is primarily controlled by the sympathetic system. Therefore, all options provided are incorrect.
